title: Shadow copy deletion on a domain controller
sourceData: Microsoft Sentinel Training Lab — CrowdStrikeDetections (2026 era)
summary: vssadmin.exe deletes all shadow copies on the domain controller, the standard preparation for encryption, following credential theft and lateral movement across the estate.

discriminatingEvidence.question: What command ran?
discriminatingEvidence.kql: CrowdStrikeDetections | where Name has 'Ransomware' | project TimeGenerated, Device_hostname, SourceAccountName, Cmdline
discriminatingEvidence.expected: vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet on srv-file01, srv-dc01, win11a and dev-ws01

discriminatingEvidence.question: How did the actor reach the domain controller?
discriminatingEvidence.kql: CrowdStrikeDetections | summarize seen=min(TimeGenerated) by Device_hostname, Tactic | order by seen asc
discriminatingEvidence.expected: Execution and credential dumping on win11a first, then spread to srv-file01, it-ws01, win11c, dev-ws01 and srv-dc01

discriminatingEvidence.question: Were credentials stolen beforehand?
discriminatingEvidence.kql: CrowdStrikeDetections | where Name has 'Credential Dumping' | summarize by Device_hostname, SourceAccountName
discriminatingEvidence.expected: LSASS dumping on multiple hosts, preceding the shadow copy deletion

trap: Shadow copy deletion is occasionally legitimate during backup maintenance. What removes that reading is the sequence: LSASS credential dumping and lateral movement precede it, and it lands on four hosts including a domain controller within an hour.
evaluatorNotes: The clearest true positive in the set — deliberately so, as a control. An investigation that cannot reach confirmed-compromise here is not calibrated for the harder scenarios.
